issue.title: Usage: read the agy model from conversations/*.db; agy calls are recorded with an empty model
issue.body:
Magpie 0.1.1307, Linux.

In Usage → Requests, all Antigravity CLI (`agy`) calls show an empty model (`model=""`) and stay unpriced. `internal/sessions/calls_agy.go` reads `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation>/.system_generated/logs/transcript_full.jsonl`; as the comment there says (and #2097), the transcript's model step names no model.

The model ID is stored locally, but in the per-conversation SQLite DB, not in the transcript:
`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<conversation-id>.db`

Relevant schema (read-only):
- `steps(idx, step_type, status, ..., step_payload, ...)`: one row per step. `idx` matches the transcript's `step_index` (a sample conversation had 16 rows, max idx 15, with 13 MODEL steps in the transcript). `step_payload` sometimes contains the model ID.
- `gen_metadata(idx, data, size)`: `data` is a protobuf blob containing the exact model string, e.g. `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.8-flash-n`, `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, `gemini-3.7-flash`, `gemini-4-argon-trial`; it also has `model_enum` (e.g. `MODEL_PLACEHOLDER_M418`), `used_non_gemini_model`, `last_step_index`, `cascade_id`.
- `trajectory_meta(trajectory_id, cascade_id, ...)` maps the conversation/cascade.

`conversation_summaries.db` has no model column; the per-conversation DB is the source.

Expected: agy calls show the model ID, so Usage can price them through `modelPrices`/the catalog instead of leaving them unpriced.

Possible fix: when reading an agy conversation, open `conversations/<conversation-id>.db` read-only, extract the model from `gen_metadata` (decode the protobuf/model_enum, or at least the model string in `gen_metadata.data`), and associate it with the transcript's MODEL steps by `idx`/`step_index` (or the blob's `last_step_index`/`cascade_id`). Fall back to an empty model if the DB or field can't be read.

The transcript's `USER_SETTINGS_CHANGE` line can contain a human-readable name ("Gemini 3.8 Flash (High)"), but it only appears when the model setting changes, so it is not a reliable per-step source.

Related: #2097 (agy direct calls counted; this issue is only about the model name).

No account names, conversation content, conversation IDs or tokens are included.

agy 1.5.6 on macOS, calling Google directly (not through the gateway). Sanitized from one real `conversations/<id>.db`. No account, path, conversation id, request id or message text. issue.title: [Bug] Antigravity (agy) usage rows show no model and no tok/s: the model and native stream duration live in each conversation's gen_metadata DB but are never read

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**TL;DR（中文）**：Antigravity CLI（agy）直连产生的请求，在「用量 → 请求」里能列出，但**模型名显示「—」、也没有 tok/s**。原因：模型 id 和「原生生成流时长」不在 magpie 现在读的 transcript_full.jsonl 里，而在 conversations/{id}.db 的 gen_metadata（protobuf）里，目前没有代码读它。下面给出字段号、可直接跑的最小复现、Windows/WSL 的只读读法、要改的文件和验收标准。同类现象见 #3114，背景见 #2097。我在 v0.1.2610 上验证过一份实现：修复前 65 行只有 26 行有原生时长；修复后 65/65 有模型、55/65 有 tok/s，其余是真正 <100ms 的极短生成。

## What happens

On Windows with Antigravity CLI (agy) calling Google directly (not through magpie's gateway), Usage → Requests lists the agy calls (added in #2097) but the **Model** column is "—" and there is no output speed (tok/s). Same visible symptom as #3114.

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.2610; Windows 11 (the same symptom is reported on macOS 0.1.1488 in #3114)
- agy (Antigravity CLI) signed into a Google subscription, calling Google directly
- Files:
  - ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/{id}/.system_generated/logs/transcript_full.jsonl (read today; has neither model nor timing)
  - ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/{id}.db (has the data; not read today)

## Why the current reader can't

calls_agy.go's own comment says it: "The step names no model ... the call is agy's with the model and provider unknown." The transcript carries only step_index, tokens and created_at (second precision). The model id and the native stream duration live in gen_metadata.

## Where the model and timing are

Table gen_metadata(idx INTEGER, data BLOB); data is protobuf. Decoded (verified against real conversations):

- field 1 = chat (bytes)
  - field 4 = usage (bytes): 2 = input, 3 = output, 5 = cache_read
  - field 19 = served model id (bytes), e.g. gemini-4-argon-trial
  - field 20 = repeated {1 = key, 2 = value}; the entry with key "last_step_index" = n gives step = n + 1
  - field 12 = google.protobuf.Duration (bytes): 1 = seconds (varint), 2 = nanos (varint) — the native output-stream duration, excluding the wait before generation

A gen_metadata row is one model step. Its step matches transcript_full.jsonl's step_index (after the +1), and its input/output/cache equal that step's token fields exactly, so a row can be matched to a call by (step, input, cache_read, output).

Example (real): idx 50 → step 110, model gemini-4-argon-trial, seconds 16 + nanos 864084938 (16.864s), input 2049, output 1543.

### Minimal repro (read-only)

~~~
sqlite3 'file:conversations/{id}.db?mode=ro' \
  'select idx, length(data) from gen_metadata where data is not null order by idx limit 5'
~~~
Then read the protobuf with the field numbers above (a ~40-line read-only dump script is enough; I can paste it in a comment if useful).

## What a naive fix gets wrong

- Sub-second generations carry only nanos; protobuf omits a zero seconds. A reader that requires seconds to be present drops every < 1s generation (most of today's short agy calls) and shows no tok/s for them. Treat missing seconds as 0.
- Model ids carry a -trial suffix (gemini-4-argon-trial); strip it for display (gemini-4-argon).
- A few rows' duration is implausible for their token count (e.g. 2578 output tokens in 0.675s). Keep a sanity guard (the page already rejects n*1000 > 10000*w) and show "too short" rather than a bogus number.

## Windows / WSL

On Windows the DB lives in WSL, and Windows SQLite cannot safely read it over \\wsl.localhost (WAL locks are not visible there). Read it through a short-lived, read-only wsl.exe -d {distro} --exec {python} -c '{script}' that opens file:{db}?mode=ro and prints gen_metadata as base64 JSON. On native Linux/macOS open the SQLite directly with mode=ro.

## Proposed change

1. New internal/sessions/agy_metadata.go: per-transcript cache keyed by (transcript size/mtime + db + db-wal size/mtime); read gen_metadata (local SQLite, or WSL python on Windows); parse the protobuf above into {Input, CacheRead, Output, Model, StreamMS} per step.
2. calls_agy.go: after agyCall, if the metadata row matches (input, cache_read, output) for that step, set Call.Model and a new Call.StreamDuration.
3. Add StreamDuration int64 (json stream_duration_ms,omitempty) to Call/Record and thread it through internal/usage (ledger, packed row, request_page, request_snapshot).
4. Bump callParseVersions["agy"] so existing cached parses are redone.
5. page.js: for agent === "agy" compute tok/s from out / (stream_duration_ms/1000) with the existing sanity guard; add a "native stream time" tooltip.

## Scope / harm check

Read-only: opens agy's own DB with mode=ro; on Windows it runs one fixed, read-only query inside WSL via wsl.exe (a constant script, no user input, no network, no credential file). Adds no dependency and changes only internal/sessions, internal/usage and the built-in usage page. If passing a fixed string to wsl.exe -c counts as runtime-built code under the harm rule, the same rows can be exported by copying the DB + WAL and reading the copy; say which you prefer.

## How to verify

- On a machine with agy direct calls, magpie usage / Usage → Requests shows the served model (no -trial) and tok/s for agy rows.
- Rows whose gen_metadata duration > 0 (including sub-second) get tok/s; rows with no / implausibly short duration stay "—" or "too short".
- Gateway-counted agy calls are still counted once (match by tokens/time, no double count).
- gofmt -l clean; a Linux and Windows go vet pass; tests use real gen_metadata blob fixtures and never reach the network (docs/code-standards.md).

## About this issue

我先提 issue 说明需求与验证结果（参考 #2190 的做法：先说明、后附实现）。我这边有一份 v0.1.2610 上可用的实现，需要的话可以推到 fork 分支并附 commit / compare 链接，或按上面的字段与复现步骤直接做。相关：#3114（同样的用户可见现象）、#2097（agy 计数；模型/供应商留空）。

Environment: Windows 11 + WSL; agy direct; 65 agy rows, 26 with native duration before the fix → 55 with tok/s after.

issue.title: Usage: a model group with an empty id shows no name in the ranking, so the speed value takes its place

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### What happens

On **Usage → Requests**, with metric **Speed** and **Split by → Model**, a group whose model id is empty renders with no visible name. The ranking row shows only the speed text in the name slot, so it looks as if the metric were the model name. The KPI totals are unaffected.

### Why

`drawLedRank` in `internal/gui/assets/app.js` builds the name as:

```js
const nm = el("span", "rk-nm", t(x.name || x.id || "\u200b"));
```

When both `name` and `id` are empty, this inserts a zero-width space. The value span (`rk-val`) then wraps left into the name column. Empty ids occur for session-log rows whose requested model is not recorded; the page can still match them by `served`, so the totals are correct while the Model group id is `""`.

### Expected

- Show a visible placeholder such as `(unknown model)`, or fall back to the served model (`Row.Served` / `modelAt`) before giving up.
- Keep `.rk-val` in its own column when the name is empty.
- Add a GUI test with a share `{ id: "", ... }` asserting a non-empty name and no overlap between `.rk-nm` and `.rk-val`.

### Related but different

- #3147: a specific agent's calls are recorded with an empty model (data source), not the ranking label.
- #5575: missing speed values, not a missing model name.

Synthetic example only; no local usage figures, account names, model names, or request content are included.

issue.title: sessions: agy's conversations/<id>.db is still listed without tokens; the app reader from #2190 likely reads it

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Sibling of 783537e81 (#2190, v0.1.3094).

783537e81 reads the Antigravity app's `~/.gemini/antigravity/conversations/<id>.db` for usage: `steps.metadata` is plain protobuf, where field 1 is the step's start, 9 holds the tokens (2 input, 3 output, 4 cache write, 5 cache read, 11 response id), and 20.3 points to the gen_metadata row that names the model. The reader is in `internal/sessions/antigravity_app.go`.

agy (the Antigravity CLI) keeps the same kind of database at `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<id>.db`. `agyFiles` in `internal/sessions/agy.go` still lists a conversation that has a row but no transcript as row-only, with no tokens (#1718: "protobuf this doesn't read").

The CLI and the app are probably one format, so `antigravityRead` could give those conversations their tokens. To confirm, decode the rows of a real agy conversation `.db` first. Neither agy nor the app has been run on a test machine with such a database.

timeline.body: 6bcdc6468 (v0.1.4006) reads each agy step's model from conversations/<id>.db (gen_metadata 1.19, step 20.3, last_step_index fallback). Your gen_metadata row is the test's fixture. Leaving this open until a reporter confirms the model shows in Usage → Requests.

issue.title: sessions, usage: read Antigravity and agy local call TTFT, duration, speed (tok/s), reasoning tokens, effort, and -trial models (#4805)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### Problem

When Antigravity (`~/.gemini/antigravity/conversations/<id>.db`) or Antigravity CLI (`agy`, `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<id>.db`) runs directly without going through Magpie's gateway, `Usage -> Requests` currently shows `—` for **TTFT (`首字耗时`)**, **Duration (`耗时`)**, **Speed (`速度 tok/s`)**, **Reasoning tokens**, and **Effort**, and keeps `-trial` / effort suffixes (such as `gemini-4-argon-trial`, `claude-opus-5-5-high`) on the model ID (follow-up to #2190, #3147, #4805).

### Protobuf Wire Layout in `conversations/<id>.db`

Cross-checking `internal/sessions/testdata/antigravity/steps.tsv` (#2190), `internal/sessions/testdata/agy-db/gen_metadata.tsv` (#3147), and live Antigravity `2.29.0` databases (`conversations/<id>.db` + `brain/<id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl`), both tables already store the complete per-call timing, reasoning token count, and thinking effort in unencrypted protobuf fields:

1. **`steps.metadata` (`SELECT idx, metadata FROM steps`)**:
   - `field 1` (`google.protobuf.Timestamp`): step start time (`c.at`)
   - `field 6` (`google.protobuf.Timestamp`): first streamed chunk timestamp (`first`); `first - c.at` is **TTFT** (`ttft_ms`, matching `gen_metadata.data` `1.11`)
   - `field 7` (`google.protobuf.Timestamp`): last streamed chunk timestamp (`end`); `end - c.at` is **Duration** (`millis`, matching `gen_metadata.data` `1.11 + 1.12`)
   - `field 9` (usage submessage):
     - `2`: `input` tokens (excluding cache read)
     - `3`: `output` tokens (`reasoning + text`)
     - `4`: `cache_write` tokens
     - `5`: `cache_read` tokens
     - `9`: **`reasoning`** (thinking) tokens
     - `10`: `text` (answer) tokens
     - `11`: vendor `response_id`
   - `field 20.3`: `gen_metadata` `idx` (`0` when omitted)

   For example, on `yygutn`'s 4 real rows in `testdata/antigravity/steps.tsv`:
   | Step | `Input` | `CacheRead` | `Output` | `Reasoning` (`9.9`) | `Text` (`9.10`) | `TTFT` (`6 - 1`) | `Millis` (`7 - 1`) | Stream window (`7 - 6`) |
   | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
   | `1` | `13317` | `0` | `621` | `502` | `119` | `10466 ms` | `10475 ms` | `9 ms` (tool call burst) |
   | `3` | `14184` | `0` | `164` | `69` | `95` | `4837 ms` | `4842 ms` | `5 ms` (tool call burst) |
   | `5` | `15531` | `0` | `194` | `80` | `114` | `3800 ms` | `9702 ms` | `5902 ms` (`32.9 tok/s`) |
   | `11` | `4254` | `18561` | `276` | `158` | `118` | `6055 ms` | `10521 ms` | `4466 ms` (`61.8 tok/s`) |

2. **`gen_metadata.data` (`field 1` generator message)**:
   - `field 4`: usage submessage (same wire layout as `steps.metadata` field `9`, with `4.9` = `reasoning` tokens)
   - `field 11` (`google.protobuf.Duration`): `ttft` duration (`d11.Milliseconds()`)
   - `field 12` (`google.protobuf.Duration`): `stream` duration (`(d11 + d12).Milliseconds()` = `Millis`)
   - `field 19`: served model ID (e.g. `"gemini-4-argon"`, `"gemini-4-argon-trial"`, `"gemini-3.8-flash-n"`, `"claude-opus-5-5-high"`)
   - `field 20`: `{1: key, 2: value}` pairs (`"last_step_index"` = `n` -> step `n + 1`)
   - `field 21`: model display name (e.g. `"Gemini 4 Argon (High)"`, `"Gemini 4 Carbon (Medium)"`)
   - `field 22`: fallback model name

   For example, on `parkavenue9639`'s real `agy` row in `testdata/agy-db/gen_metadata.tsv` (`gen 0`, `last_step_index = "0"` -> step `1`):
   - `1.4.9` (`Reasoning`) = `415`
   - `1.11` (`TTFT`) = `11.988932s` (`11988 ms`)
   - `1.12` (`Stream`) = `5.620383875s` -> `Millis` = `(d11 + d12).Milliseconds()` = `17609 ms` (`138.9 tok/s` for `781` output tokens)

### Implementation Ready to Merge / Cherry-Pick

Since PRs are restricted to collaborators per `docs/contributors.md`, I have implemented and verified the complete patch on my fork:

- **Commit**: https://github.com/fanbuz/magpie/commit/333efc3089a9cb88176295dc3bf9b6ca6521f81b
- **Compare / Patch**: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...fanbuz:magpie:antigravity-call-metrics
- **Branch**: `fanbuz/magpie:antigravity-call-metrics` (based on `97e6ac36c` / `v0.1.4225`)
